sources.entry: Product Manager Skills — PM-focused skill pack

summary.one_liner: A Markdown-based skill pack that turns AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf) into a product-manager assistant for PRD critique, SaaS metric diagnostics, roadmapping, discovery, and career coaching.
summary.what_it_does: The repo is a set of human-readable Markdown knowledge modules, templates, and routing logic that an AI coding tool loads as a skill. It covers discovery and research (JTBD, Mom Test, opportunity solution trees), strategy and prioritization (RICE, ICE, Kano, TAM/SAM/SOM), and artifacts such as PRDs, user stories, and PRFAQs. It also includes a finance module that calculates SaaS metrics like churn, LTV, CAC payback, and Rule of 40 from raw numbers, plus growth/PLG and career-coaching modules. A "coaching mode" pushes back on weak framing, and a 6-phase "PM Sprint" workflow runs from idea to PRD. The README says it ships 7 knowledge modules, 12 templates, 8 worked examples, and two small shell scripts for manual maintenance.
use_cases: Critique a PRD before sharing it with engineering
Diagnose SaaS health from MRR, churn, and CAC figures
Pressure-test a roadmap against stakeholder requests
Turn a vague feature idea into a problem statement and PRD draft
Prepare for PM-to-Director interviews and leadership coaching
Plan customer discovery interviews and experiments
how_to_run: Claude Projects: upload SKILL.md, knowledge/, and templates/
Any LLM with local file loading: point the system prompt at SKILL.md and keep sibling folders intact
notable: Workflow-first design: outputs decisions, tradeoffs, assumptions, and a completion status instead of generic text
Built-in SaaS metric calculator covering 32 metrics, with worked churn/LTV/payback example
Explicit anti-pattern checks such as solution smuggling, metrics theater, and feature factory
PM Sprint workflow chaining Discover, Position, Prioritize, Specify, Validate, Measure phases
No auto-executed code at runtime; the optional scripts are for manual maintenance
caveats: Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which restricts commercial use
README says it is not for teams wanting a collaborative web app with approvals, comments, or sharing
Requires an AI coding tool or LLM that can load local files; no standalone app is described
